methodological_rigor.justification: Single-center prospective observational screening study of 54 adult P/LP TP53 carriers with two WB-MRI scans 12 months apart, 93% adherence for the second scan, and standardized 1.5T scan protocol (T1 DIXON, T2 HASTE, DWI b=50 and 900) reviewed independently by two experienced onco-radiologists scored 0-5 in monthly MDM. Strengths include prospective design, dual-reader review, and TNM staging. Weaknesses: no control group (unlike the earlier SIGNIFY comparator), arms were excluded from field of view (contributing to interval cancers), and sample size was empirically chosen without formal power calculation. Descriptive statistics only (medians, percentages), no inferential testing, and no formal sensitivity analyses or adjusted detection rate estimates.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Prospective case series/cohort without contemporaneous control, mapping to Oxford LoE 4. Findings directly inform LFS surveillance policy in the UK: 16.7% (9/54) cancer detection rate overall with 70% early-stage and curatively treated, supports annual WB-MRI implementation alongside breast MRI. The paper contextualizes against SWEP53, LIFSCREEN, SMOC+, Villani cohort and two meta-analyses (Ballinger; Temperley), strengthening clinical guidance.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational study; STROBE is the applicable reporting standard and the manuscript includes a 'STROBE diagram' in Figure 1 (although labeled CONSORT in the text, creating confusion). Eligibility, setting, variables, outcomes, and limitations are covered. Data availability is limited: supplementary URLs are redacted, no open-data or individual-participant-level deposition is described, and some denominators (ECOG status at scan 2) contain minor percentage inconsistencies (e.g., 23/50=46% vs 4/50 'Not carried out' labeled 6%).

novelty_literature.justification: The value of WB-MRI in LFS surveillance has been demonstrated in SIGNIFY (UK), SWEP53 (Sweden), LIFSCREEN (France), SMOC+ (Australia), Villani cohort (Canada), and confirmed in two meta-analyses. SIGNIFIED's specific contribution is being the first prospective UK study with two annual WB-MRI scans (rather than single baseline), highlighting interval cancers and operational barriers to NHS implementation. Meaningful practice-oriented extension rather than first-in-class.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear structure with narrative case descriptions, helpful tables of demographics (Table 1), and cancer/treatment outcomes (Table 2). Limitations and implementation barriers (scanner access, radiographer expertise, registries) are candidly discussed. Minor issues include a figure mislabeled as 'STROBE diagram' while the caption refers to CONSORT, a typo in a figure caption ('cut-o' instead of 'cut-off'), and some demographic denominator inconsistencies.

key_strengths: First UK prospective study with two annual WB-MRI scans in LFS; 93% adherence for second scan
16.7% overall cancer detection (10 cancers in 9 patients) with 70% diagnosed at early stage
Dual-reader radiology review and monthly MDM adjudication with standardized scoring (0-5) and TNM staging
Candid discussion of five interval cancers and practical NHS implementation barriers
key_concerns: Single-center, no contemporaneous control, and descriptive-only statistics without confidence intervals or inferential testing
Arms excluded from WB-MRI field of view contributed to interval cancer missed (e.g., upper limb sarcoma)
31% (17/54) of participants had prior WB-MRI, confounding interpretation of baseline detection rate
Figure/text inconsistency labeling STROBE vs CONSORT diagram; minor demographic denominator inconsistencies
No data availability statement or deposition described
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically important, well-conducted UK screening cohort in an ultra-rare syndrome with meaningful cancer detection and policy-relevant findings, limited by descriptive-only statistics and absence of control, placing ceiling at tier 2 with minor revisions.
